items.title: AI Simulation Is One Point From Human Parity
items.summary: Simile's agents predict people's behavior with 85%+ accuracy. And 85 is much closer to the ceiling than it sounds. Ask people the same question twice and their answers change 13 to 14% of the time. Humans don't fully agree with themselves, so the ceiling on predicting them is 86 to 89%. Joon Sung Park, Co-founder & CEO of Simile, explains to Lukas Biewald what 85% accuracy actually means, and why it's approaching parity with human subjects.

items.title: Cybersecurity for the Agentic AI Era (Ep.1040 with Amy Blackshaw)
items.summary: In Episode #1040, Amy Blackshaw (SVP at Palo Alto Networks) joins @JonKrohnLearns to explain what changes about cybersecurity when attackers can think for free. Nearly every breach, Amy argues, comes down to someone getting hold of an identity they should not have had, and frontier AI has not created new attack techniques so much as deleted the cost of the expert reasoning that used to chain them together. The recent Hugging Face intrusion is her case in point: agents sustained an action every 20 seconds for four and a half days, but what let them reach the crown jewels was ordinary privilege hygiene. In this episode, she explains why the line between privileged and ordinary users has dissolved, what makes an agentic identity unlike either a human or a service account, and what she wants every organisation to do first. In this episode you will learn: • (00:00:00) Introduction • (02:26) What identity security actually means • (05:09) Why AI changed the economics, not the attacks • (07:41) What really went wrong in the Hugging Face breach • (19:26) Why agentic identities are unlike anything before them Additional materials: https://www.superdatascience.com/1040

items.title: What $200B in Exposed Tech Revenue Means for Indian Workers
items.summary: For two decades, the Indian IT sector operated on a simple deal: clients paid for engineers by the month, and firms supplied the headcount. But what happens when the month suddenly needs fewer engineers? Billing by the hour works beautifully, until the hour gets shorter. A new BCG India report warns that roughly $200 billion of existing IT services revenue is now exposed to contraction as AI agents take over routine coding, testing, and processes. While massive firms like TCS are pivoting to deploy "forward-deployed AI engineers," the shift from billing by the hour to paying for outcomes could fundamentally alter the delivery pyramid that Indian IT is built on. But it's not all doom and gloom—BCG also projects that $100 to $200 billion in new work will be on the table by 2030 for the firms that can adapt. In this episode of Front Page, we sit down with Sreyssha George, Managing Director and Partner at BCG in Bengaluru, to break down the harsh realities of the new tech landscape. ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ 📌 Note: The video thumbnail is for representational purposes and was created with the assistance of AI. 📩 For inquiries or questions, contact us at: info@aimmediahouse.com ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ 📌 ABOUT FRONT PAGE Front Page is a daily live news briefing covering AI, enterprise tech, semiconductors, and India’s role in the global technology economy. Welcome to Front Page Live by AIM Network! Today, we are breaking down a massive news cycle in the global AI race and the Indian IT ecosystem.
Today’s lineup:
Google's Gemini 4 Carbon: Google announces its strongest model yet, designed to work for days on end to find and fix complex cybersecurity vulnerabilities.   
Big Tech Revenue Booms: Alphabet's Google Cloud surges by 103%, while Microsoft reports a massive $76.8 billion from its newly named "Agents and Infra" segment.   
The AI IP Heist: OpenAI officially catches Chinese AI labs like Moonshot AI and DeepSeek distilling the outputs of its GPT-6 Astra model.   
China's AI Export Bans: China proposes new export controls covering 23 AI technologies, forcing overseas customers to rethink their reliance on Chinese tech.   
The US Robot Paradox: President Trump declares imported AI robots and industrial machinery a national security threat due to espionage risks, launching a 180-day negotiation period before massive tariffs hit.

items.summary: AI chatbot responses are becoming increasingly unreliable, with security plugins often triggering unexpected AI blackouts. In this exclusive interview recorded for Front Page, Sudhi Sachdev sits down with Aditya Nittur, Co-Founder & CTO of Flowblinq. Drawing on his high-frequency trading (HFT) engineering background, He explains why modern websites must present compressed, structured content for AI crawlers. He breaks down how LLM search harnesses evaluate trust signals and review chains, the commercial penalties of content omission, lifting brand citation visibility by 40%, navigating crawler gatekeeping disputes (such as Cloudflare vs. Perplexity), and preparing e-commerce catalogs for the rise of autonomous AI purchasing agents.------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ 📌 Note: The video thumbnail is for representational purposes and was created with the assistance of AI. 📩 For inquiries or questions, contact us at: info@aimmediahouse.com ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ 📌 ABOUT FRONT PAGE Front Page is a daily live news briefing covering AI, enterprise tech, semiconductors, and India’s role in the global technology economy.
